Thanks <@552133098075193354> 🙏 https://x.com/TimBeiko/status/1965047756386644270 Forkcast has added protocol calls , including transcripts & chatlogs. 👏 <@119818938845495298> PSA: transcripts & chatlogs also cover before YouTube stream is live. https://x.com/wolovim/status/1965439884262523183 forkcast - protocol calls Can we discuss uncapping the deposit/withdrawal queues in Glamsterdam back to the old system where it scaled with the total amount of ETH staked? 43 days to withdraw is just bad mechanics & UX plus with consolidations now in full swing, the arbitrary 256 ETH limits no longer seem necessary and sre actually counterproductive. At the very least, we should lift the churn cap on the withdrawal queue. This trades off against the weak subjectivity period, no? The reason for the 256 ETH hard cap was the validator set was growing too fast. This is no longer the case. Even if that is a concern (I dont think it is personally), no reason to keep withdrawal capped at 256 ETH/epoch still. the cap on withdrawals isn't related to the validator set growing too fast, it's about weak subjectivity and the hit to that with the introduction to consolidations The choices are being fine with the weak subjectivity loss, or reducing the churn allocated to consolidations Considering the consolidations operation barely getting any use (most are just withdrawing and redeposit as 0x02 validators), is this even a worthwhile tradeoff? It would be helpful to understand what *all* staking pools think about this, since so little of the stake has been consolidated at this point. If it is indeed the case that this is what everyone is planning to do, it could make sense to reduce the consolidation churn in favor of exit churn Considering the earliest this change could happen is Glamsterdam and that about at least a year away but we are scoping it out now, definitely something to be actively considered.

excerpts.author: greystroke
excerpts.content: Can we discuss uncapping the deposit/withdrawal queues in Glamsterdam back to the old system where it scaled with the total amount of ETH staked? 43 days to withdraw is just bad mechanics & UX plus with consolidations now in full swing, the arbitrary 256 ETH limits no longer seem necessary and sre actually counterproductive.  At the very least, we should lift the  churn cap on the withdrawal queue.
